disputes.issue: Original E14 showed Hartwell attrition flat (6 vs 5 prior year), within the 3-8 historical range, and other sites flat; a careful reader could defensibly answer 'contradicted' (evidence counts against an increase), so 'unknown' was not uniquely defensible. Blind answer was 'contradicted'.
disputes.resolution: Reworded E14: Hartwell leavers 9 vs 5 (just above historical range) while other sites flat, plus a Hartwell-specific confound (better-paying 300-seat contact centre opened locally in June; leavers' next employer not recorded; 3 exit interviews split pressure/pay/relocation). Rise rules out 'contradicted', the local rival rules out 'supported'; 'unknown' now unique. Updated I5 and I12 rationales and narrative.

disputes.issue: With flat attrition (original E14) A3 addressed an apparently non-existent problem, making 'acceptable' or 'harmful' arguable against 'premature'.
disputes.resolution: Resolved by the E14 rewrite: attrition now plausibly elevated but causally unresolved, so A3 is right only if H5 is confirmed -> 'premature' unique. Expected answer unchanged.

disputes.issue: Blind choice was Q1, Q3. Q3 (review of released calls) bears on H2, which is already established, so it is not discriminating; Q2 targets the only open hypothesis H5. Q2's value was weak when attrition was flat.
disputes.resolution: Kept [Q1, Q2]; E14 rewrite makes Q2 clearly discriminating. Q3 left neutral (neither discriminating nor low-value).
